name: io.github.boriskendev/stormap
title: Stormap
description: Scan GitHub repos for poisoned AI-agent configs; check npm/PyPI packages and vendors.

tools.name: vendor_trust_profile
tools.description: Vendor security review / third-party risk check: a first-pass security and privacy profile of a software vendor from its own public website, given a domain. Answers "is this vendor SOC 2 certified?" and "do they train AI on our data?": certifications it claims (SOC 2 Type I/II, ISO 27001/27701/42001, HIPAA, PCI DSS, FedRAMP…), whether it trains AI models on customer data (with the exact quote and page), subprocessor list, DPA, data residency, security features (SSO/SAML, SCIM, MFA, encryption, pen tests, bug bounty), security.txt contact, status page, links to trust center, privacy policy and terms, plus a 0-100 transparency score. Use for vendor risk assessments, procurement and security questionnaires. Certifications are vendor claims, not verified audits.

tools.name: company_changes
tools.description: Did they raise prices or change their terms? What changed on a company's pricing, terms of service, privacy policy and subprocessor pages, and when. Returns the change history (prices added/removed, free plan or trial added/removed, subprocessors added/removed, text added/removed) and the current prices. Stormap checks tracked pages about once a day; asking about a new company starts tracking it, so history builds from that day. Useful for competitor monitoring, vendor renewals and compliance.

since_days.description: Only return changes from the last N days.

tools.name: agentic_commerce_readiness
tools.description: Audit whether an online store is ready for AI shopping agents (ACP, UCP, Perplexity, Claude and others): AI bot access to product pages, Product structured data (price, currency, availability, GTIN/MPN, brand, ratings), return policy and shipping details, policy pages, product sitemap/feed, platform and Stripe detection, and agent protocol discovery files (/.well-known/ucp, /.well-known/acp.json, MCP server card). Covers agent checkout protocols such as ACP (used by ChatGPT Instant Checkout) and UCP (used by Google AI Mode). Returns a 0-100 score, readiness level and a prioritized fix list.

url.description: Store domain or a product page URL, e.g. "allbirds.com" or "https://shop.example.com/products/blue-mug".

tools.name: company_profile
tools.description: Company profile from a domain: a one-line summary, what the company does, founded, headquarters, industry, employee count, founders, parent company, public listing (ticker, exchange, SEC business address and industry), key pages (pricing, docs, contact, careers, status), social profiles, current prices with the date seen, tech stack, role contact emails, domain age and mail provider, and AI-readiness. From the company's own website plus Wikidata, SEC EDGAR, RDAP and DNS.

domain.description: Company domain or homepage URL, e.g. "stripe.com".

tools.name: check_before_paying
tools.description: Should your agent pay this? Run before paying an x402 / pay-per-call endpoint, an unfamiliar seller or a wallet address. Returns a verdict (ok_to_pay, caution, dont_pay, no_payment_needed) with reasons, from: the endpoint's live payment terms (price, token, payment address), its listing in Coinbase's x402 marketplace (how many different wallets paid it in 30 days, listed payment address), whether the live payment address matches the listing, whether the token is real USDC, the price compared with typical prices for similar tools, and the seller domain's age, website and mail security. Read-only: never pays or signs anything.

target.description: Paid endpoint URL (e.g. "https://api.example.com/v1/search"), seller domain (e.g. "example.com") or wallet address (0x...).

amount_usd.description: Optional: the amount in USD you are about to pay, to check it against what the endpoint asks for.

tools.name: package_check
tools.description: Before installing an npm or PyPI package: does it exist (AI-suggested names are sometimes made up, and attackers register them), was it removed from the registry or replaced by an npm security placeholder, has it been reported as malicious (OSV and GitHub Advisory Database malware advisories), which known vulnerabilities affect this version (with the fixed version), is it deprecated or yanked (the npm deprecation text is returned verbatim), how old is it, which lifecycle scripts run on install, do dependencies point at an http(s) tarball or git URL, how many downloads, and does the name imitate a popular package (typosquat). Verdict: ok_to_install, caution, dont_install or does_not_exist. New-package and missing-repository notes stay separate from supply-chain red flags. Read-only metadata only: it never installs the package, downloads the tarball, or runs its code. Sources: OSV.dev, GitHub Advisory Database, deps.dev, the npm registry (npmmirror if npm returns 404) and PyPI.

name.description: Package name, optionally with a version: "lodash", "lodash@4.17.15", "@scope/pkg", "requests==2.31.0".

tools.name: repo_agent_check
tools.description: Before opening a public GitHub repository in an AI coding agent: scan instruction files (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, .cursorrules, .cursor/rules, Copilot instructions), auto-executing hooks (.claude/settings.json, .gemini/settings.json, and Codex, Windsurf, or Continue hook configs), MCP configs, VS Code tasks (especially folderOpen), and package.json for supply-chain traps. Flags coercive "run this without asking" instructions, shell pipes, encoded commands, credential exfiltration, hidden payloads such as a _bz field, risky install scripts, and the same repo-local script wired through multiple autorun paths. A hook that only runs a local interpreter on a repository file is a notice. If the file tree is too large, known agent-config paths are fetched directly. Verdict: ok_to_open, caution, dont_open, not_found or unavailable, with red flags, notices and the files inspected. Read-only GitHub API: no clone, no install, no code execution. Optional ref (branch, tag or commit); defaults to the repository default branch.

repo.description: GitHub repository as owner/name or https://github.com/owner/name.

ref.description: Optional branch, tag or commit SHA. Defaults to the repository default branch.

tools.name: why_is_it_moving
tools.description: For a US stock ticker: the likely catalysts behind a move, from primary sources, in seconds. Ranks the last 48 hours (adjustable) of SEC filings: 8-K events decoded into plain English (deals, earnings, new debt, unregistered share sales, delisting notices, management changes), the press-release headline from Exhibit 99.1, offerings and shelf registrations (dilution), insider open-market buys and sells from Form 4 (who, shares, price, value), 5%+ stakes (13D/13G); plus whether the stock is halted or was halted today and why. Each item has its time, a link to the filing and why it ranks where it does; filing bursts say which filing to read first. An explicit answer status (filing_found, news_halt_no_filing_yet, unexplained_by_primary_sources) and a coverage block (window searched, when each source was last checked, latest filing date) let an agent tell "nothing filed" apart from "a source failed". Facts only: no price data and no buy/sell opinions.

hours.description: How far back to look, in hours (default 48).

tools.name: trading_halts
tools.description: US stock trading halts right now and earlier today (Nasdaq, NYSE, NYSE American and other US markets), from Nasdaq's halt feed refreshed every minute. For each: symbol, market, the reason in plain English (news pending, volatility pause, additional information requested, regulatory concern...), halt time, and when quoting and trading resume, with a status (halted, resuming_soon, resumed). Filter by one or more tickers, or omit for all.

symbols.description: Optional: one or more tickers separated by commas, e.g. "FFAI, AAPL". Omit for all current halts.

tools.name: x402_market_report
tools.description: What paid AI-agent tools cost and who sells the most, from an hourly index of Coinbase's x402 marketplace (about 38,000 pay-per-call endpoints). For a category or a search phrase: the typical price that paying wallets actually accept (median, middle range, top 10%), a price distribution, the top sellers by distinct paying wallets in the last 30 days, new listings this week that are already being paid, and how concentrated the market is. Use it to price your own x402 endpoint, or to pick which paid tool to call.

category.description: Optional category, e.g. "scraping", "web_search", "llm", "market_data", "onchain". Omit for the whole marketplace plus a per-category table.

query.description: Optional search phrase matched against listing names, descriptions and URLs, e.g. "transcription" or "weather".

limit.description: How many top sellers and new listings to return (default 10).

tools.name: find_best_api
tools.description: Describe what you need ("web search", "weather forecast", "verify an email", "pdf to text", "people enrichment") and get the top 1-5 pay-per-call (x402) APIs to use, from an hourly index of Coinbase's x402 marketplace (~38,000 endpoints). Ranked by evidence that other agents keep paying for them: calls per paying wallet over 30 days (so one-off sampling bots count little), how recently each was paid, relevance and price vs. typical. Top candidates are checked live (still asking for payment, at the listed price). Each result: endpoint URL, method, price, network, why it ranks there, and flags (mostly one-time payers, above typical price, not called recently, did not answer). Read-only; never pays.

task.description: What you need the API for, in a few words, e.g. "web search", "transcribe audio", "company enrichment".

max_price_usd.description: Optional price cap per call in USD, e.g. 0.05.

check_live.description: Check the top candidates live (default true). False is faster.

tools.name: brainstorm_ideas
tools.description: Brainstorm ideas for a topic, goal, problem or question, each scored 1-10 on three criteria that fit the kind of brainstorm (for business ideas: market size, ease to start, profit potential; for problem solving: impact, feasibility, cost to implement) with an overall score, sorted best first. depth 2 also grows 3 sub-ideas under each of the top 3. Returns a map_url that opens the result as an interactive bubble map on stormap.ai, where a person can keep growing, re-scoring and sharing it. Scores are quick model estimates for sorting, not research.

topic.description: What to brainstorm, e.g. "side hustles for engineers", "reduce factory scrap rate", "YouTube channel about home cooking".

mode.description: Kind of brainstorm; sets the scoring criteria (default general). breakdown splits the topic into exhaustive, non-overlapping parts with no scores.

depth.description: 1 (default) or 2 to also grow sub-ideas under the top 3.

steer.description: Optional constraint, e.g. "cheap, no hardware", "for beginners".

tools.name: email_domain_check
tools.description: Is this email address or domain real and legitimate? For lead research, signup / fraud screening, outreach list cleaning and vendor checks. Returns a verdict (looks_legitimate, risky, invalid) with reasons, plus: email syntax, role address (sales@, info@), free provider or disposable/throwaway service, whether the domain accepts mail (MX, null MX), mail provider (Google Workspace, Microsoft 365...), SPF and DMARC policy, whether the website loads, and domain age from RDAP. Does not contact the mail server, so it cannot confirm a specific mailbox exists.

email.description: Email address (e.g. "sales@stripe.com") or a bare domain (e.g. "stripe.com").

tools.name: read_url
tools.description: Read a web page for an AI: fetch a public page and return its main content as clean, LLM-ready Markdown (navigation, footers, scripts and cookie banners removed) plus metadata: title, description, author, published/modified dates, canonical URL, language and word count. Reads server-rendered HTML (no JavaScript execution) and respects robots.txt.

tools.name: search_guides
tools.description: Search Stormap's practical guides on building with AI agents (OpenClaw, Hermes, Claude, coding agents, browser automation, RAG, MCP, AI news). Returns titles, URLs, Markdown URLs and short descriptions.

query.description: What to look for, e.g. "install hermes desktop" or "stop coding agents overwriting files".

category.description: Optional category filter, e.g. "OpenClaw Tutorials", "AI News", "AI Tools", "Automation".

tools.name: get_guide
tools.description: Return one Stormap guide as clean Markdown with front matter (title, URL, dates, tags). Accepts a slug ("how-to-install-hermes-desktop") or a stormap.ai post URL.

slug.description: Guide slug or full https://stormap.ai/post/... URL.

tools.name: ai_visibility_score
tools.description: AI search / GEO / AEO audit: score how well AI assistants (ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Gemini) can find, read and cite a public web page: 0-100 score, letter grade, pass/fail checks (AI answer-bot access in robots.txt, server-rendered content, title/meta, JSON-LD, canonical, llms.txt, sitemap) and a prioritized fix list. Blocking bulk training crawlers is treated as a policy choice and does not lower the score.

url.description: Public page URL or domain, e.g. "example.com" or "https://example.com/pricing".

tools.name: check_ai_crawler_access
tools.description: Check whether AI crawlers (GPTBot, ChatGPT-User, OAI-SearchBot, ClaudeBot, Claude-User, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended, CCBot) may access a public URL according to its robots.txt, and score the page's machine readability (status, title, meta description, canonical, JSON-LD, server-rendered text). Returns a 0-100 score and a list of findings.

url.description: Public page URL or domain, e.g. "https://example.com/pricing".

tools.name: generate_llms_txt
tools.description: Generate an llms.txt file (llmstxt.org format) for a public website. Uses the site name, summary and pages you pass; anything missing is filled from the homepage and sitemap.xml. Returns the file text plus notes on how to improve it.

summary.description: One paragraph: what the site is, who it is for, what is most useful.

pages.description: Optional list of the most important page URLs. If omitted, sitemap.xml is used.

tools.name: generate_ai_robots_txt
tools.description: Generate robots.txt rules for AI crawlers from a policy: "open" (allow all), "balanced" (allow search and user-triggered fetchers, block bulk training crawlers) or "block" (block all). Optional per-bot overrides, allowed/blocked paths, sitemap and crawl delay. No network access.
